THOUGHT: Key features point strongly to a dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) phenotype. The patient has a chronic (>10 years), localized, intensely pruritic, lichenified papular/plaquelike eruption on the shin with milia and areas of erosion/partially detached epidermis. Histology shows a subepidermal (dermoepidermal) split and milia in the superficial dermis — consistent with a subepidermal blistering disorder and typical of EB. Crucially, whole-exome sequencing found a novel heterozygous COL7A1 missense variant (c.6832G>T, p.Gly2278Trp) with cosegregation, and COL7A1 encodes type VII collagen (mutated in dystrophic EB). The clinical presentation (adult onset, localized pretibial distribution, pruritic lichenified/nodular lesions with milia) fits the pruriginosa/pretibial phenotype of dominant DEB. Autoimmune subepidermal blistering disorders (epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, bullous pemphigoid/lichen planus pemphigoides) can produce similar histology and milia but are less likely given the confirmed germline COL7A1 variant and long-standing familial course. Porphyria cutanea tarda and other photodistributed blistering disorders are less consistent with the site and lack of other features (photosensitivity, lab abnormalities). Therefore the top diagnosis is dominant dystrophic EB (pruriginosa/pretibial phenotype); remaining entities are listed as reasonable differentials in descending likelihood.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB), dominant type — pruriginosa/pretibial phenotype (COL7A1 heterozygous missense mutation)  
2. Localized (pretibial) dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (clinical/descriptive variant of DEB)  
3. Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (autoimmune anti–type VII collagen disease)  
4. Bullous lichen planus / lichen planus pemphigoides (interface dermatitis with secondary subepidermal blistering)  
5. Localized bullous pemphigoid (atypical, pretibial presentation)
